castle.observation: For ordinary non-missile actor targeting, spelltargets tests the selected party or monster condition and Rand(100) below 34 before the selected monster's above-100 magic-resistance exclusion. Success tracks q[up], the active caster, instead of the selected actor. resolvespell then rolls and resolves only the effective tracked target, so the caster may still resist or save; the original actor is not also affected. cast invokes this independently for every target-type-zero selection. Monster getrange and target sampling include opposed party actors and opposed monsters in native slots ten onward. If reflection kills a monster caster, killbody queues its macro while inspell remains true; combat.c does not test caster stamina between noofmagattacks iterations, and getup drains the queue only after that spell loop completes. Monster damage calls killbody whenever stamina is nonpositive, not only on the transition, so another reflected hit appends another record for the same caster to Castle's fixed 100-entry todoque.
unresolved: Automatic target types 9, 10, and 12 branch before the per-cell reflection test and therefore do not inherit ordinary reflection.

Area targeting can encounter one actor through multiple footprint cells and intelligent monster scoring invokes spelltargets in mode true, consuming reflection RNG before the actual cast; those suspicious source effects remain disabled.
Queued-field collisions pass noreflect true and remain a separate persistent-field contract.
Monster cannot value four reverses allegiance for friendly targeting and remains disabled as its own spell-targeting branch.

providence.expectedRepresentation: Schema v2 already preserves ordinary target type, spell resolution fields, and all forty signed monster starting conditions. Reflection is runtime condition behavior and requires no new package field.

cases.claim: Race and caste character values are one-based Classic identities 1 through 30, each resolves file record identity minus one, and the same identity indexes display names and race-to-caste eligibility.

remake.behavior: Remake retains one-based character race/caste values and subtracts one before looking up active rule records and name arrays.

castle.observation: Race and Caste initialize character values to one, present up to thirty name slots, and pass those values to loadprofile. loadprofile subtracts one record before seeking each fixed table, while Race copies all thirty can-caste columns by zero-based record index.

providence.expectedRepresentation: Schema v2 contains exactly thirty races and castes with unique classicId values 1 through 30, stable IDs classic.race.N and classic.caste.N, imported display names, and eligibility references using those same identities.
